name: 2100 Prairie Avenue — Sherman Victorian Gothic (district draft; refined by T-1919, T-1920)

grade.why: Pictured: 3 of the pictures on the Images tab show it.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 21.000, v -2.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation -0.614 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 2100 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2100 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: '3S.B.' printed on the 1911 sheet: 3 full storeys.

construction.note: The register reads the map's colours as 'brick'.

s35fp-2100-b1 p2 (range, frame), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 68% of its fill

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s35fp-2100-b1 p1 (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 88% of its fill; s35fp-2100-b1 p2 (range, frame), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 68% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row '(default)' overlaid with the frontage row: The John B. Sherman house (Burnham & Root, 1874), standing empty in 1904 after Sherman's death: the register's 'steep slate roof and stone dormers' and 'carved chimney tops' as a steep hip with dormers and three stacks over the 3S.B. brick body, the curved stair and clustered columns as a central entrance. The 1911 lettering McCORMICK MEDICAL COLLEGE is a later use and is not drawn; the oriel on its column is T-1919's. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 1346818164 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-west-2351.

value.card: District draft — refined by T-1919, T-1920.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet labels the building with a 1911 use, '3S.B. brick building lettered McCORMICK MEDICAL COLLEGE, on the 21st Street corner', which the draft does not carry back to 1904 (the T-1837 register warns not to assume the 1904 use from it). The register's family row, 'Sherman Victorian Gothic', names it a house, so the 1904 function is inferred residence on that row and the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The marker: 'John B. Sherman Residence. Built 1874'.

citations.citation: 'Lost Houses of Prairie Avenue: 2000-2100 Blocks', Prairie Avenue Historic District interpretive marker, Chicago; transcription on the Historical Marker Database (HMdb), marker 308703.

what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2351, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1919, T-1920 refine in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2100-b1), the T-1842 census (s35-2100-front, s35-2100-wing, s35-2100-walls) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-064 (Sherman Victorian Gothic); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-west-2351).
